newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian royal tit-for-tat over succession remarks.
newsitem.headline: Belgian royal tit-for-tat over succession remarks.

text.p: The Belgian royal palace reacted sharply on Wednesday to remarks made by King Albert's disgruntled youngest son Laurent that the country's previous King manoeuvred him out of the line of succession.

A book published earlier this month claimed that King Baudouin, who died childless in 1993 and was succeeded by his brother Albert, personally took the initiative to change the constitution to prevent Laurent from becoming king.

Laurent was second in line, after his older brother Philippe, until he was leapfrogged by his older sister Astrid -- and her four children -- in 1991 when parliament approved a constitutional change to permit women to accede to the throne.
Laurent told Het Laatste Nieuws last weekend he had been aware of the news in the book by prominent political analyst and emeritus professor Jean Stengers.
"I have been suffering from this situation for years," Laurent, a dog lover who last year wrote a book on the role of mans' best friend through the ages, told Belgian media earlier this week.

But the Palace, quoted by Belgian media from Oslo where the king and queen are on an official visit, said the constitutional change had been open and correct and had been considered by parliament since 1978.
The Palace, which rarely comments on affairs involving royals, also noted that equality of men and women has been a basic principle of society which had already been followed by other monarchies.
Albert is Belgium's sixth king since the dynasty was formed in 1831.
